learning_objective: 🎯 To look closely at the objects around us, learn what they are made of, and discover how scientists sort them by their special properties!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Look at your pencil! It is made of wood and graphite. A bottle might be plastic or glass. The stuff used to make any object is called a material. One object can even be made of many different materials!
Materials have special features or 'properties'. Some are super hard like iron, some are soft like sponge, some shine brightly (lustre), and others let light pass right through them (transparent)!
If you drop a coin in water, it sinks to the bottom. But a dry leaf will float on top! Scientists group materials based on whether they are heavier or lighter than water.

fun_activity.title: 💧 The Great Dissolving Race
fun_activity.instructions: Take two glasses of water. Put a spoon of sugar in one and a spoon of sand in the other. Stir them both and observe which material disappears (is soluble) and which stays at the bottom!

quick_recap: ⭐ Objects are made from a wide variety of materials like wood, glass, metal, and plastic.
⭐ We group materials together based on their shared properties, like appearance, hardness, and transparency.
⭐ Some materials dissolve completely in water, while others do not.
